metaDescription: Six bath transfer boards and benches compared on stated weight limits, tub width fit, seat type and drainage, with advice to confirm setup with a therapist.
introParagraphs: A bath transfer board spans the edge of a tub so the user can sit down outside it and shift across to bathe, instead of stepping over the wall. There are two broad styles. A bath board is a seat that rests across the tub rim, and a transfer bench adds legs, a backrest and a seat that extends outside and inside the tub. The two differ in stability, in how much support they offer and in how well they suit users who cannot lift their legs over the tub wall.

This lineup covers six products from DMI, Drive Medical, PEPE Mobility, FinityPro, Buckingham Healthcare and suboton. Stated capacities run from 242 pounds on the Pepe to 400 pounds on the DMI bench, and tub width fit ranges are stated on several listings. We evaluated each from its product page and listing specifications, comparing capacity, tub fit, seat style, drainage and weight. A wet, soapy tub raises the fall risk, so all of this is a comparison of equipment and not clinical advice.

Ask a physical or occupational therapist to assess your bathroom and to teach the transfer before first use. Measure the inside width of your tub, confirm the stated weight limit with margin and check that every foot sits firmly on the tub floor or the bathroom floor.

products.name: DMI Tub Transfer Bench with Backrest

specList.label: Overall size
specList.value: 39 W x 18 D x 37 H inches

products.description:
The DMI is a full transfer bench and the highest-rated product in this comparison at 400 pounds. It has a rust resistant aluminum frame, a blow molded seat with a backrest, a hook and loop safety belt, nylon strap locks that hold the seat and suction cup rubber feet. The seat has a removable cutout for perineal access and a handle for extra stability while showering.

It is built for users who need to sit down outside the tub and slide inside, so it can help someone who cannot lift their legs over the wall. The listing says the seat can be configured for a right or left install and that the bench is tool free and freestanding with no permanent mounting. Seat height adjusts from 19 to 23.5 inches, and the overall size is 39 inches wide, 18 inches deep and 37 inches tall.

It weighs 10.7 pounds, nearly double the 5.5 pound Pepe board, so it is harder to remove from the tub. The listing notes that the product contains latex, which matters for anyone with an allergy. Compared with the 350 pound Drive bench, it offers a higher rating and a safety belt, but the Drive adjusts in finer steps. A therapist can confirm the setup for your tub.
products.bestFor: Users who need full support, a backrest and the highest stated capacity here.
pros: 400 lb stated capacity, the highest here
Seat height adjusts from 19 to 23.5 inches
cons: 10.7 lb is heavy to remove from the tub
Large 39 inch width needs bathroom room

products.name: Drive Medical Tub Transfer Bench, 350 lb
products.description:
The Drive Medical bench is an aluminum tub transfer bench with a comfortable backrest and a stated capacity of 350 pounds. The listing describes height adjustable legs supported by dual column extensions that adjust in 0.5 inch increments. It also mentions drainage openings and suction cup feet meant to add stability.

The fine height steps are the main practical advantage. A seat that sits level with the tub rim and with the user's own chair makes the slide easier and safer, and half-inch steps let you fine tune it. The backrest supports users who tire sitting upright while bathing. The listing does not give an overall size or a weight in the information we reviewed, so confirm those on the product page before buying.

At 350 pounds it states 50 pounds less than the DMI bench and 50 pounds more than the Pepe's roughly 242. It has no safety belt in the listing, unlike the DMI. Check that the legs lock fully at the chosen height. A therapist can help you set the seat height and positioning for a safe transfer.
products.bestFor: Users who need a backrest and want to dial in seat height precisely.
pros: 350 lb stated capacity with an aluminum frame
cons: Overall size and weight not in the listing
350 lb limit is below the DMI at 400 lb

products.name: PEPE Mobility Bath Board with Handle, Model 2
products.description:
The Pepe is a simple bath board that rests across the tub and has a handle, four adjustable non-slip legs and drainage holes. It is made of polypropylene, weighs about 5.5 pounds and states a maximum user weight of 242 pounds. The listing says it fits tubs between 15.5 and 24.5 inches wide, measured between the inner walls.

Its light weight makes it easy to lift out and leave the tub free, which is the main advantage over a bench like the 10.7 pound DMI. The listing is clear about its limits. It is recommended for users with upper trunk control who do not need a caregiver, and for greater limitation it points buyers to a swivel chair or a transfer bench.

The 242 pound rating is the lowest in this lineup, well below the 400 pound DMI and the 350 pound Drive. It has no backrest, so the user sits on a flat board with a handle. The listing says to measure the tub before buying, and that is the key step. A therapist can confirm that a board without a backrest is safe for the user.
products.bestFor: Lighter users with good trunk control and a tub within the 15.5 to 24.5 inch range.
pros: 5.5 lb weight is easy to remove from the tub
Clear tub width range of 15.5 to 24.5 inches
cons: 242 lb maximum user weight is the lowest here
Meant for users who do not need a caregiver

products.name: FinityPro Rotating Tub Transfer Bench with Handle
products.description:
The FinityPro is a bath board with a 360 degree rotating seat and a safety handle. It states a 300 pound capacity and fits tubs between 18 and 26.5 inches wide, with a listed weight of 5.6 pounds. The listing says it is easy to wipe clean and portable enough to install and remove at home or in a hotel.

The rotating seat lets the user sit facing out and then turn to face into the tub without lifting their legs over the wall, which is its main selling point. A rotating seat also adds speed and a moving part, so it should be tried with a therapist or helper before anyone uses it alone. Its tub width range of 18 to 26.5 inches starts 2.5 inches wider than the Pepe's 15.5 inches and ends 2 inches wider.

At 300 pounds it states more than the 242 pound Pepe but less than the 350 pound Drive and 400 pound DMI. It has no backrest in the listing. Check the rotation for smooth, even movement before each bath, and measure your tub first. A therapist can advise whether a rotating seat suits the user.
products.bestFor: Users who benefit from a seated turn and have a tub in the 18 to 26.5 inch range.
cons: Rotating mechanism adds speed and parts to check
300 lb limit is below the benches

products.name: Buckingham Healthcare Glideboard Transfer Board
products.description:
The Buckingham Glideboard is a polymer board with a sliding seat that the listing says detaches for cleaning. It measures 27.75 by 13.5 by 0.75 inches and states a 300 pound capacity. The listing mentions contoured edges, handles and a design that works around wheelchair handles, and says it was developed with an occupational therapist's input.

The listing describes it as a bath board and a wheelchair transfer board, and it says both the board and the seat can be cleaned with soap and water, which suits a wet bathroom. The sliding seat is meant to reduce friction compared with a traditional plain board. At 13.5 inches wide it is the widest board in this group, wider than the 8 inch plain boards, which gives the user a larger seat surface.

It is a board and not a bench, so it has no legs or backrest and does not adjust to a tub. It rests between surfaces and relies on them being firm, which matters over a wet tub rim. It states the same 300 pounds as the FinityPro but offers a detachable seat for cleaning. A therapist can confirm whether it suits your bathroom layout and how to position it safely.
products.bestFor: Wheelchair users who want a wide, easy-clean gliding seat that works beyond the bathroom.
pros: 13.5 inch width gives a broad seat
Detachable seat cleans with soap and water
cons: Board only, with no legs or backrest
Needs firm surfaces on both sides
Does not adjust to tub width

products.name: suboton Transfer Board with Slide Sheet 31.5 in
products.description:
The suboton is a general-purpose transfer board that the listing says can be used for wheelchair to car, toilet or tub transfers. It comes with a 31.5 by 8 inch board and a 28 by 28 inch slide sheet. The board has three handles, curved edges and an anti-slip design on the back.

Unlike the benches and the Pepe, this is not a bath-specific product. It does not rest on the tub rim and sit above the water, so it suits transfers between a wheelchair and a shower chair or tub seat, not bathing on the board itself. The listing information we reviewed does not state a weight capacity, so confirm that on the product page before buying.

Its 31.5 inch length is the longest of the plain boards here, and its three handles give more grip points than the Buckingham. It has no backrest, no legs and no drainage, so it should not be left wet. Dry it after any bath-area use. A therapist can show you how to combine the board with a slide sheet safely.
products.bestFor: Users who need a board to reach a shower chair or tub seat and also use it elsewhere.
pros: Includes a 28 by 28 inch slide sheet
31.5 inch length reaches across wider gaps
cons: Not a dedicated bath board or bench
Weight capacity not in the listing information

buyingCriteria.explanation: A bath board rests across the rim and offers a seat, while a transfer bench has legs, a backrest and a seat that sits outside and inside the tub. The DMI and Drive Medical are benches, the Pepe and FinityPro are bath boards and the Buckingham and suboton are transfer boards. Users who cannot lift their legs over the tub wall or who tire sitting upright usually need a bench with a backrest. A board suits users with good trunk control.

The stated capacity is the maximum load the maker rates the product for, and wet bathrooms add a reason to leave margin. The DMI bench states 400 pounds, the Drive 350, the FinityPro and Buckingham 300 and the Pepe 242. Choose a limit comfortably above the user's weight. If a listing gives no figure, as with the suboton, confirm it before buying.

A board or bench must span the tub with its feet or ends resting firmly. The Pepe fits tubs from 15.5 to 24.5 inches wide, and the FinityPro fits 18 to 26.5 inches. Measure the inside width between the walls at the rim before buying. A product that only just fits can shift under load.

A bench must sit level, and a seat at the wrong height makes the slide harder. The Drive adjusts in 0.5 inch steps, the DMI from 19 to 23.5 inches and the Pepe has four adjustable legs. Suction cup feet and non-slip legs help, but they work only on clean, dry surfaces. Check that every foot is locked and flat.

Some households leave the tub free for others and need to remove the product each time. The Pepe at 5.5 pounds and the FinityPro at 5.6 pounds are easy to lift out, while the DMI at 10.7 pounds is heavier. A bench like the DMI is 39 inches wide and needs bathroom room. Think about who will move it and where it will be kept.

Wet bathrooms need materials that drain and wipe clean. The Pepe and Drive list drainage holes or openings, the Buckingham seat detaches for cleaning, and the DMI uses rust resistant aluminum. The DMI listing notes that it contains latex, which matters for allergy. Dry boards that are not made for the tub after use.

howWeEvaluated.title: Stated capacity
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared the weight limits each listing gives, from 242 pounds on the Pepe to 400 pounds on the DMI. We noted where a listing gave no figure. The DMI and Drive lead on capacity among the benches.

howWeEvaluated.title: Tub fit and sizing
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared stated tub width ranges, such as 15.5 to 24.5 inches on the Pepe and 18 to 26.5 inches on the FinityPro, and overall dimensions such as the DMI's 39 inch width. Products with a clear fit range scored higher.

howWeEvaluated.title: Seat style and support
howWeEvaluated.description: We separated benches with backrests from boards without, and noted rotating and gliding seats. The DMI and Drive offer the most support, while the Pepe offers the least. We weighed support against bathroom room.

howWeEvaluated.title: Adjustability and stability features
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at height adjustment, non-slip feet, belts and handles. The Drive leads on fine adjustment with 0.5 inch steps, and the DMI adds a safety belt and handle.

howWeEvaluated.title: Weight, cleaning and drainage
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared weights from 5.5 pounds on the Pepe to 10.7 pounds on the DMI, and drainage and cleaning notes. The Pepe and FinityPro are the easiest to remove, and the Buckingham seat is the easiest to detach and clean.

faq.q: What is the difference between a bath board and a transfer bench?
faq.a: A bath board rests across the tub rim and gives a seat, while a transfer bench has legs, a backrest and a seat that reaches outside and inside the tub. The DMI and Drive are benches, and the Pepe and FinityPro are boards. A bench suits users who cannot lift their legs over the wall. A therapist can advise which fits.

faq.q: How do I measure my tub?
faq.a: Measure the inside width between the walls at the rim, and compare it with the stated fit range. The Pepe fits 15.5 to 24.5 inches and the FinityPro 18 to 26.5 inches. A product at the edge of its range may shift under load. Confirm the fit on the product page before buying.

faq.q: Are these safe on a wet tub?
faq.a: Wet surfaces reduce grip, so check that every foot sits flat and that suction cups are on clean, dry areas. The DMI and Drive list suction cup feet, and the Pepe lists non-slip legs. Never use a product beyond its stated limit. A therapist can assess your bathroom.

A backrest helps users who tire sitting upright or need more support. The DMI and Drive have one, while the Pepe and FinityPro do not. The Pepe listing says it is meant for users with upper trunk control who do not need a caregiver. A therapist can say whether a board without a backrest is safe.

faq.q: Is the DMI bench safe for latex allergy?
faq.a: The DMI listing says the product contains latex. Anyone with a latex allergy should avoid it or ask the seller for details. Other products here do not state this in the information we reviewed. Confirm materials on the product page.

faq.q: How do I clean and dry these products?
faq.a: Rinse and wipe them after each use and let them dry. The Buckingham seat detaches and cleans with soap and water, and the Pepe and Drive have drainage. Dry any board not made for the tub, such as the suboton, after use. Inspect feet for wear.

faq.q: Can I use these without a caregiver?
faq.a: Some users with good balance and strong upper limbs transfer alone, but bathrooms carry a real fall risk. The Pepe listing says it suits users who do not need a caregiver, while other products suit assisted use. A physical or occupational therapist can assess your situation. If there is any doubt, have a helper present.
